title: Alex Van Halen: The Hard Rock Archetype - Modern Drummer
notes: Modern Drummer, 2 February 2012 (read through a summary of the page). His "incessant (and sometimes slightly swung) 16th-note beats on his hi-hat", "blanketing crash-ride hiss, and throaty, conga-esque snare sounds"; influenced by "Mitch Mitchell, Keith Moon, Ginger Baker, and Bonham"; played "as though he were 'viciously attacking something'"; "I'm the first to admit that I push the beat. The idea of trying to create strict metronomic time is nonsense." Hot for Teacher's "hard-driving double bass shuffle from hell"; in the 1980s "electronic drum pads" added to the kit; Unchained among the cuts named.

title: Icons of Rock: Alex Van Halen - Consequence
notes: Alex Young, 18 October 2008. "Alex added a second bass drum to his kit, creating a double bass tower behind which he was a monster"; his idols Ginger Baker and Keith Moon; Hot for Teacher's "thunder-like double bass".

title: 1970 Ludwig Pro Beat - Silver Sparkle - Van Halen Gear Timeline
notes: A fan history of his kits, no author or date. A 1970 Ludwig Pro Beat in silver sparkle, 14x24 kick, a Supraphonic snare; expanded to a seven-piece double-bass kit, the second kick 14x26 from 1975; a 6.5x14 Super Sensitive the main snare "into the early 80s"; front heads off the bass drums, muffled with felt, foam and tape; Zildjian cymbals; used on the first two albums (Sunset Sound, 1977 and 1978).

title: Women and Children First - Wikipedia
notes: Van Halen's third album, March 1980, produced by Ted Templeman; Alex Van Halen, drums.

title: Everybody Wants Some!! (song) - Wikipedia
notes: A "jungle" drum and Tarzan-like vocal introduction; the drum-vocal breakdown improvised; the band later used its opening drum beat as the way into Panama.

title: Jump (Van Halen song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at 5150 by Donn Landee and Eddie Van Halen; the synthesiser an Oberheim OB-Xa; 129 beats per minute; Alex Van Halen, drums.

title: Panama (Van Halen song) - Wikipedia
notes: The published score in E major at 144.

title: Hot for Teacher - Wikipedia
notes: "The song features Alex Van Halen's double bass drum performance"; the 30-second drum intro, a double-kick half-time shuffle reminiscent of Cobham's Quadrant 4 and Simon Phillips's Space Boogie; Drumeo's breakdown: rudiments on a Simmons pad for the first six bars, then triggered double bass and rototoms.
